offer_letter.markdown:
# Offer of employment — Head of Islamic Banking (Principal)

## 1. Our offer to you

Dear {{employee.full_name}}, we are pleased to offer you the job of Head of Islamic Banking (Principal) at Absa Group. This is a permanent position. Your first day will be 1 December 2026. Your place of work will be Sandton, head office.

## 2. What you will do

You will define and execute the Islamic Business Banking strategy. You will grow the business, customer base and market proposition. You will drive commercially sustainable Shari'ah-compliant banking solutions, lead product and proposition innovation, and strengthen customer and stakeholder relationships. You will navigate Shari'ah governance, risk, regulatory and control requirements, partner across Product, Distribution, Operations, Risk, Compliance, Finance and Digital, and build and lead a high-performing Islamic Banking capability. We may also ask you to do other reasonable duties that fit the position.

## 3. Pay and working hours

Your basic salary is R18,000.00 per month. We pay on the 25th of each month by EFT. We will deduct PAYE and UIF of 1%. You will work 40 hours a week, 8 hours a day over 5 days, Monday to Friday from 08:00 to 17:00, with a 60-minute meal interval. Any overtime is by agreement and is paid at 1.5 times your ordinary hourly wage.

## 4. Leave and probation

You get 15 working days of paid annual leave in each 12-month leave cycle. You also get 30 days' paid sick leave in every 36-month cycle and 3 days' family responsibility leave a year. Maternity leave is at least 4 consecutive months and parental leave is 10 consecutive days. The first 3 months are a probation period, during which we will assess your performance and give you support.

## 5. How to accept

Please reply by 30 November 2026. Send your ID and your qualifications to hr@example.co.za. If you have any questions, please use the same email address.

## 6. Acceptance

I, {{employee.full_name}}, accept this offer of employment. Signed on {{date_signed}}.

contract.markdown:
# Contract of employment — Head of Islamic Banking (Principal)

## 1. Parties

This contract of employment is entered into between Absa Group, of 1 Main Road, Sandton (the Employer), and {{employee.full_name}}, identity number {{employee.id_number}}, of {{employee.address}} (the Employee).

## 2. Position and duties

The Employer appoints the Employee as Head of Islamic Banking (Principal). The Employee's duties include: Define and execute the Islamic Business Banking strategy.; Grow the business, customer base and market proposition.; Drive commercially sustainable Shari’ah-compliant banking solutions.; Lead product and proposition innovation.; Strengthen customer and stakeholder relationships.; Navigate Shari’ah governance, risk, regulatory and control requirements.; Partner across Product, Distribution, Operations, Risk, Compliance, Finance and Digital.; Build and lead a high-performing Islamic Banking capability.. The Employer may reasonably require the Employee to perform other duties consistent with the position.

## 3. Commencement

Employment commences on 1 December 2026 on a permanent basis.

## 4. Probation

The first 3 month(s) of employment are a probationary period during which the Employer will assess the Employee's performance against the requirements of the position and give reasonable evaluation, instruction, training, guidance or counselling where needed. Confirmation, extension or termination at the end of probation will follow a fair procedure.

## 5. Place of work

The Employee's place of work is Sandton, head office.

## 6. Hours of work

The Employee's ordinary hours of work are 40 hours per week, 8 hours per day over 5 days per week (Mon–Fri 08:00–17:00). A meal interval of 60 minutes is taken after no more than five hours of continuous work. The Employee is entitled to a daily rest period of at least 12 consecutive hours and a weekly rest period of at least 36 consecutive hours.

## 7. Remuneration

The Employee will be paid R18,000.00 per month (basic salary), equivalent to R103.85 per ordinary hour, payable monthly on the 25th by EFT. No other cash payments are payable. No payments in kind are made.

## 8. Overtime

Overtime is worked only by agreement and may not exceed ten hours in any week. Overtime is paid at 1.5 times the Employee's ordinary hourly wage, or, by agreement, compensated with paid time off. Work on a Sunday is paid at double the ordinary wage (or one and a half times if the Employee ordinarily works on Sundays), and work on a public holiday at double the ordinary wage.

## 9. Deductions

The following deductions will be made from the Employee's remuneration: PAYE; UIF 1%. No other deduction will be made without the Employee's written agreement in respect of a specific debt, or as required by law, a court order or an arbitration award.

## 10. Leave

The Employee is entitled to 15 working days of paid annual leave per annual leave cycle of 12 months, to be taken at a time agreed with the Employer and not later than six months after the end of the cycle. Sick leave: 30 days' paid sick leave in every 36-month cycle (during the first six months, one day for every 26 days worked); a medical certificate may be required for absences of more than two consecutive days or on more than two occasions in eight weeks. Maternity leave: at least 4 consecutive months. Parental leave: 10 consecutive days. Adoption and commissioning parental leave as provided in the Act. Family responsibility leave: 3 days' paid leave per year once employed for longer than four months and for at least four days a week.

## 11. Termination and notice

Either party may terminate this contract on written notice of one week if the employee has been employed for six months or less; two weeks if employed for more than six months but not more than one year; four weeks if employed for more than one year. Notice may not be given during any period of leave. Nothing in this clause prevents the Employer from terminating employment summarily for a fair reason following a fair procedure, or the parties from agreeing to waive notice.

## 12. Bargaining council or sectoral determination

No bargaining council agreement or sectoral determination applies to the Employer's business.

## 13. Confidentiality

The Employee will not, during or after employment, disclose or use any confidential information of the Employer, its clients or suppliers, except as required to perform the Employee's duties or by law.

## 14. Other documents

No other documents form part of this contract.

## 15. General

This contract records the whole agreement between the parties on its subject; any amendment must be in writing and signed by both parties. Where any term is less favourable to the Employee than the Basic Conditions of Employment Act or an applicable sectoral determination or collective agreement, the more favourable provision applies. The Employer will keep these particulars for three years after termination and will explain them to the Employee on request.

## 16. Signatures

Signed at ____________ on {{date_signed}}.

For the Employer: {{employer.signatory}}  ____________________

The Employee: {{employee.full_name}}  ____________________

plain_language.explanation: This says who the agreement is between. The employer is Absa Group, at 1 Main Road, Sandton. You are the employee, named with your identity number and your address.

You are appointed as Head of Islamic Banking (Principal). Your duties are listed, including setting and running the Islamic Business Banking strategy, growing the business, driving Shari'ah-compliant solutions, leading innovation, building relationships, handling Shari'ah governance, risk, regulatory and control needs, partnering across Product, Distribution, Operations, Risk, Compliance, Finance and Digital, and leading the Islamic Banking team. The employer may also reasonably ask you to do other duties that fit this position.
Your employment starts on 1 December 2026. The job is permanent, so it has no end date.

Your first 3 months are a probation period. During this time the employer will assess your performance against the job requirements and give you reasonable evaluation, instruction, training, guidance or counselling where needed. At the end, your job can be confirmed, probation extended, or your employment ended, and a fair procedure must be followed.
You will work at Sandton, head office. That is your place of work under this contract.

You work 40 hours a week, 8 hours a day, over 5 days, Monday to Friday from 08:00 to 17:00. You take a 60-minute meal break after no more than five hours of non-stop work. You also get at least 12 hours of rest in a row each day and at least 36 hours of rest in a row each week.
You are paid R18,000.00 per month as basic salary, which works out to R103.85 per ordinary hour. Payment is made monthly on the 25th by EFT. No other cash payments and no payments in kind are made.

You only work overtime if you agree to it, and it cannot be more than ten hours in any week. Overtime is paid at 1.5 times your ordinary hourly wage, or you can agree to take paid time off instead. Sunday work is paid at double your ordinary wage (or one and a half times if you normally work Sundays), and public holiday work is paid at double.
PAYE and UIF of 1% will be taken off your pay. No other deduction may be made unless you agree in writing for a specific debt, or the law, a court order or an arbitration award requires it.

You get 15 working days of paid annual leave for each 12-month leave cycle, taken at a time agreed with the employer and no later than six months after the cycle ends. You get 30 days' paid sick leave in every 36-month cycle, but in your first six months you earn one day for every 26 days worked, and a medical certificate may be asked for if you are off more than two days in a row or more than twice in eight weeks. Maternity leave is at least 4 consecutive months, parental leave is 10 consecutive days, adoption and commissioning parental leave are as set out in the Act, and you get 3 days' paid family responsibility leave a year once you have worked longer than four months and work at least four days a week.

Either you or the employer can end the contract with written notice: one week if you have worked six months or less, two weeks if more than six months but not more than one year, and four weeks if more than one year. Notice cannot be given while you are on leave. The employer may still dismiss you immediately for a fair reason using a fair procedure, and both sides may agree to skip notice.
No bargaining council agreement applies to this business. No sectoral determination applies either.

You may not share or use the employer's confidential information, or that of its clients or suppliers. This applies while you work there and after you leave. The only exceptions are when you need it to do your job or when the law requires it.
Only this contract applies. No other documents form part of it.

This contract is the full agreement on what it covers, and any change must be written down and signed by both of you. If any term gives you less than the Basic Conditions of Employment Act, a sectoral determination or a collective agreement, the better provision applies instead. The employer must keep these particulars for three years after your employment ends and must explain them to you if you ask.
This is the signature block. The employer's signatory signs for Absa Group, and you sign as the employee. It records the place and the date of signing.
